title: Production of Elastin-like Protein Hydrogels for Encapsulation and Immunostaining of Cells in 3D
protocol: Prepare ampicillin and chloramphenicol agar plates by autoclaving 25 g of Luria broth and 15 g of agar per 1 L of ultrapure water.
Add 1 mL of ampicillin stock (100 mg/mL in ultrapure water) to the cooled solution for a final concentration of 100 µg/mL.
Add 1 mL of chloramphenicol stock (34 mg/mL in 70% ethanol) to the cooled solution for a final concentration of 34 µg/mL.
Transfer 20 mL of the prepared agar solution into each 10 cm Petri dish using a serological pipette.
Allow the agar to solidify completely before wrapping the Petri dishes with parafilm and storing at 4°C.
Streak BL21(DE3)pLysS E. coli containing pET15b vector encoding the ELP of interest on an ampicillin and chloramphenicol agar plate.
Incubate the streaked plate upside down in an incubator at 37°C overnight.
Parafilm the plate after removing it from the incubator and store for a maximum of 4 days at 4°C.
Prepare a starter culture flask (250 mL) and expression culture flasks (12x 1 L).
Autoclave the prepared flasks.
For 1 L of expression media, add 47.6 g of terrific broth to ultrapure water in a 2 L baffled culture flask.
Add 4 mL of glycerol to the expression media.
Cap the flask with aluminum foil.
Load the autoclaved starter into a pre-warmed, 37 °C shaking incubator and incubate without agitation.
Add 250 µL of sterile-filtered ampicillin stock (100 mg/mL) to the starter culture for a final concentration of 100 µg/mL.
Begin agitating the starter culture at 250 rpm.
Inoculate the starter culture by adding a single ELP plasmid-containing E. coli colony from the streaked plate.
Allow the starter culture to shake at 37 °C for 16 h.
Place the expression culture media flasks into pre-warmed, 37 °C shaking incubators and incubate overnight without agitation.
Make fresh, sterile-filtered ampicillin stock (100 mg/mL in ultrapure water).
Add 1 mL of ampicillin stock to each flask of expression media for a final concentration of 100 µg/mL.
Begin agitating the expression media at 250 rpm.
Take a 2 mL sample of media and add to a cuvette as a blank for an optical density reading at 600 nm (OD600).
Inoculate each expression flask by transferring 20 mL of starter culture to each flask via a serological pipette.
Measure the OD600 of one of the expression flasks after 1 h agitation.
Measure the OD600 every 20 min, checking a different flask each time.
Reduce the temperature of shakers containing the expression flasks when an OD600 of 0.6 is reached.
Check the OD600 every 10 min once temperature reduction begins.
Induce the expression by adding 1 mL of 1 M sterile-filtered β-isopropyl thiogalactoside (IPTG) to each expression flask when an OD600 of 0.8 is reached.
Allow the E. coli in expression flasks to express for 7 h.
Pre-cool a large floor centrifuge to 4 °C, 20 min prior to the end of expression.
Collect all 12 L of expression media into individual centrifuge containers and balance.
Centrifuge the expression media at >12,000 x g for 15 min at 4 °C using a floor centrifuge.
Pour off the supernatant from each centrifuge container.
Using a spatula, collect the cell pellets into a pre-weighed zip lock bag.
Re-suspend the pellet in sterile-filtered TEN buffer.
Remove air bubbles by massaging the re-suspended pellet.
Place the re-suspended cell pellet into a secondary container.
Freeze the secondary container at -80°C overnight.
Allow the frozen pellet to slowly thaw at 4°C with gentle agitation using an orbital shaker.
Add ~30-40 mg of deoxyribonuclease I (DNase) to the thawed lysate.
Add 1 mL of 100 mM phenylmethylsulphonyl fluoride (PMSF) in isopropanol per 100 mL of cell lysate.
Allow the lysate to shake overnight.
Freeze the completely thawed lysate at -80°C overnight.
Repeat the freeze-thaw procedure for a total of three cycles.
Leave the lysate thawed at 4°C after the last freeze-thaw.
Store 100 μL of raw lysate for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Adjust the pH of the thawed lysate to 9.0 using 1 M NaOH.
Incubate at 4°C for at least 1 h on an orbital shaker.
Cool the floor centrifuge to 4°C 20 min prior to centrifugation.
Aliquot and balance the thawed lysate into centrifuge containers.
Centrifuge the samples at >15,000 x g for 1 h at 4°C.
Store 100 μL of the supernatant for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Transfer the supernatant to new centrifuge containers and balance appropriately.
Add sodium chloride (NaCl) in three parts to a final concentration of 1 M.
Agitate for 3 h at 37°C at 250 rpm in a shaking incubator.
Pre-warm a floor centrifuge to 37°C one hour before the end of agitation.
Centrifuge at >15,000 x g for 1 h at 37 °C.
Store 100 µL of the supernatant for SDS-PAGE analysis after purification completion and discard the remaining supernatant.
Re-suspend the pellet by adding 10 mL of autoclaved, ultrapure water per 1 g of pellet.
Mash the pellet with a metal spatula to aid dissolution.
Adjust the pH of the thawed lysate to 9.0 using 1 M NaOH.
Agitate overnight at 4 °C on an orbital shaker.
Centrifuge the re-suspended pellet in a pre-chilled centrifuge at >15,000 x g for 1 h at 4 °C.
Store 100 µL of the supernatant for SDS-PAGE analysis after purification completion.
Desalt the protein solution by dialyzing the remaining supernatant in a 3.5 kDa dialysis membrane against 4 L of pre-chilled ultrapure water at 4 °C.
Change the dialysis water twice a day for a total of 6 times over 3 days.
Centrifuge the dialyzed solution in a pre-cooled centrifuge at >15,000 x g for 1 h at 4 °C.
Store 100 µL of the supernatant for SDS-PAGE analysis at the end of the purification.
Freeze the resulting supernatant at -80 °C in pre-weighed conical tubes.
Lyophilize the frozen solution for 3 days and mass the final product to determine the protein yield.
Parafilm the tubes containing the final lyophilized ELP product and store at 4 °C.
Run SDS-PAGE to determine the purity of the protein.
Use a biopsy punch with the desired diameter to create holes in a 0.5 mm thick silicone sheet.
Cut out a square around each hole for the number of molds desired.
For cell cultures of 50 10^6 cells/mL, use 0.5 mm thick molds with 4 mm and 5 mm diameters respectively.
Remove plastic wrap from each side of individual mold using tweezers.
Arrange bare silicone molds and glass coverslips in alternating rows on the inverted lid of a 48-well plate using tweezers.
Cover the lid of the 48-well plate to avoid contamination.
Treat the entire 48-well plate lid with oxygen plasma.
Invert the silicone mold onto the adjacent glass coverslip immediately after plasma treatment.
Press firmly on the mold to ensure bonding.
Incubate the molds at room temperature for 1 hour.
Sterilize the molds by autoclaving.
Store the molds at room temperature in a sterile environment indefinitely.
Remove lyophilized ELP from cold storage.
Warm the protein to room temperature before opening the tube to prevent condensation.
Dissolve ELP in Dulbecco's phosphate-buffered saline (DPBS) at 4 °C with constant agitation overnight.
Dilute THPC in DPBS just prior to use.
Add 2.6 μl of THPC solution (80% in water) to 997.4 μl of DPBS.
Purge the THPC stock container with nitrogen gas.
Vortex the THPC solution and keep on ice.
Sterile filter the THPC stock solution using a 0.22 μm syringe filter.
Dilute the THPC stock solution further with sterile DPBS to achieve lower stoichiometric crosslinking ratios.
Dissociate cells by incubation with Trypsin-EDTA into a single-cell suspension.
Pellet the cells and count the cells re-suspended in medium using a hemocytometer.
Aliquot the desired number of cells into a sterile 1.5 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cells at ~200 x g for 3 min.
Aspirate the supernatant completely.
Resuspend the cell pellet in the ELP stock solution such that the volume is 80% of the final volume.
Pipette mix 20-25 times to produce a homogenous mixture of cells and ELP.
Avoid gripping the bottom of the tube to mitigate temperature increase and subsequent phase transition of ELP.
Add 6 μL of ELP stock solution and 1.5 μL of THPC stock solution into each mold, dividing equally for replicates.
Pipette mix 20-25 times to produce a homogenous mixture.
Immediately pipette the corresponding final volumes of cell/ELP/THPC mixture into each mold by a circular motion.
Incubate the samples at room temperature for 15 min.
Incubate the samples at 37 °C for 15 min.
Add 750 μL of warm cell culture medium to each well of the 24-well plate, avoiding disrupting the gels.
Incubate the hydrogels at 37 °C for 7 days.
Prepare the fixation solution by mixing 10 mL of 16% (w/v) paraformaldehyde with 30 mL of DPBS.
Warm the fixation solution to 37°C.
Aspirate the medium from the 24-well plate and gently wash each well with 1 mL of DPBS.
Add 750 µL of the fixation solution to each well.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 min, avoiding contamination by not using the tissue culture incubator.
Aspirate the fixation solution from each well and discard it into a hazardous waste container.
Add 1 mL of DPBS to each sample.
Immediately aspirate the DPBS and discard it into a PFA waste container.
Wash samples twice with 1 mL of DPBS for 10 min each.
Permeabilize each sample with 750 µL of permeabilization solution (DPBS containing Triton X-100) for 1 h at room temperature on a rocker at 15 rpm.
Aspirate the PBST and add 750 µL of blocking solution (PBS, BSA, serum, and Triton X-100) to each sample.
Incubate at room temperature for 3 h on a rocker at 15 rpm.
Prepare the antibody dilution solution by mixing 97 mL of DPBS, 2.5 g of BSA, 2.5 mL of serum, and 0.5 mL of Triton X-100.
Dilute the primary antibody using the antibody dilution solution.
Add 500 µL of the diluted primary antibody to each sample.
Seal the plate with Parafilm.
Incubate the plate overnight at 4 °C on a rocker.
Aspirate the antibody solution from each sample.
Wash the samples with PBST for 60 min at room temperature on a rocker at 15 rpm.
Repeat the wash step three times.
Dilute the secondary antibodies using the antibody dilution solution.
Dilute DAPI stock (1:2,000) in the antibody dilution solution.
Add 500 µL of the diluted secondary antibodies and DAPI to each sample.
Cover the 24-well plate with aluminum foil.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C on a rocker.
Aspirate the antibody solution from each sample.
Wash the samples with PBST for 30 min at room temperature on the rocker.
Repeat the wash step three times.
Position a drop of hard-set mounting medium onto the surface of a glass slide.
Remove excess solution from the mold by lightly blotting the edge on a paper towel.
Place the mold upside down onto the mounting medium carefully.
Allow the mounting medium to harden for 48 hours at room temperature.
Store the samples at room temperature or 4 °C.
Seal the samples to the glass cover slide with clear nail polish.
Image the samples using a confocal microscope.
